title: Cleanup GPU linker cache and lazy-init: untangle prelink/rpath complexity
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: Resolve a class of intermittent cold-start failures and large startup jitter caused by ad-hoc ldconfig/prelink/rpath interactions in our GPU serving image. The runtime currently mixes baked rpaths, on-startup prelink steps, and a lazy kernel loader that triggers ld.so cache updates. This leads to symbol shadowing across CUTLASS/Triton runtime variants and unpredictable probe order on machines with mixed driver versions. Scope: 1) Remove runtime-side ldconfig mutations and move link-time decisions into a deterministic staged-loader. 2) Split kernel bundles into stable and experimental lanes to avoid accidental symbol overrides. 3) Add an explicit rpath resolution step during package build and include a lightweight runtime fallback that uses a pinned loader path instead of relying on system ld cache. 4) Add unit and integration tests that simulate heterogenous driver/toolchain environments and validate cold-start latency and symbol resolution correctness. Why now: Recent customer incidents and CI flakiness (see perf spikes on nightly perf-gpu-2) indicate these interactions are causing production regressions. This cleanup reduces tech debt and enables safer CUTLASS/Triton upgrades going forward.
acceptance_criteria: No runtime invocation of ldconfig or equivalent; build-time rpath resolution verified in artifacts
Cold-start 95th percentile latency reduced by >=20% on heterogenous fleet synthetic benchmark
Symbol shadowing regression tests added and green in CI (unit + integration)
Kernel bundles separated into stable/experimental with explicit loader selection and documented policy
Migration guide and rollback steps published in Confluence and runbook updated
comments: 2025-02-14 — Ticket created. Initial investigation reproduces cold-start jitter on mixed-driver nodes. Captured traces in perf-grafana: dashboard 'gpu-startup-jitter' (grafana.internal/r/7Jx).
2025-02-18 — Design sync with @infra and @runtime teams. Agreed to avoid runtime ldconfig; choose staged loader approach. Action: Marco to prototype loader shim.
2025-02-22 — Prototype shows deterministic symbol resolution when loader is pinned to /opt/redwood/loader-v2. Reduced 95p cold-start from 420ms to 300ms in local mixed-driver test harness.
2025-02-25 — Security review note: loader path must be group-owned and immutable; scoped KMS key not required. @security reviewed approach and requested permissions matrix in runbook.
2025-03-01 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289 (loader shim + build-time rpath resolution). Requesting eng review and bench runs. Linked perf job: ci/gpu-loader-canary-1289.

2025-03-03 — Design review feedback: prefer splitting kernel bundles by compatibility tags (sm-* for stable, exp-* for experimental). Need a migration plan for Dedicated nodes. Added follow-up task to add autoscaler policy to prefer stable bundles for production clusters.
notes: Trade-offs: avoiding runtime ldconfig eliminates a class of flakiness but increases build-time complexity and artifact size slightly. We must maintain backward compatibility for older dedicated fleets by shipping a small compatibility shim. Long-term this enables safer CUTLASS/Triton upgrades and simpler CI determinism.
